# SK4020 — The lambda captures nothing and is not `static`

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A lambda, anonymous method or local function that references nothing outside itself can be `static`, and then it cannot allocate a closure.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Performance |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | 9.0 |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

A lambda that captures a local or `this` is compiled into a display class, and every evaluation of the lambda expression allocates one — or, where the compiler can cache it, keeps the captured object alive for the lifetime of the cache. A lambda that captures nothing has neither cost, and the compiler is free to cache one delegate instance for the whole program. `static` is the keyword that says so and the compiler that checks it: the modifier is a compile-time assertion that the body references no enclosing local, parameter, `this` or `base`, so a `static` lambda that compiles is a lambda that provably allocates no environment. That makes it the rare performance edit with no judgement in it — the fix is one keyword, the compiler verifies the claim, and a later edit that starts capturing is rejected at the point it is written instead of silently reintroducing the allocation.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
items.Select(item => item.Name);

void Sort(int[] values) {
    int Compare(int left, int right) => left.CompareTo(right);
}
```

Write:

```csharp
items.Select(static item => item.Name);

void Sort(int[] values) {
    static int Compare(int left, int right) => left.CompareTo(right);
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ The rule reports only what it can prove, and every unproven shape is declined. The body is walked in full — including nested lambdas, local functions and query clauses — and any of the following withholds the finding: `this` or `base`; a local, parameter or range variable declared outside the reported declaration, which includes a primary constructor parameter and the implicit `value` of a setter; an instance field, property, event or method reached without a receiver; a call to a local function declared outside, whose own captures this rule cannot see; and any name the semantic model does not resolve, so a file with errors reports nothing rather than guessing. Names that cannot capture are admitted: types, namespaces, aliases, labels, discards, static members, and everything inside `nameof`. Lambdas converted to an expression tree rather than to a delegate are excluded, as is any lambda nested inside one. A declaration already marked `static` is not reported, and neither is anything below C# 9. ⚠ **Disjoint from `SK4002` by construction**: that rule reports a delegate capturing iteration-local storage, and a declaration this rule reports captures nothing at all, so no declaration can produce both. ⚠ The fix does not claim an allocation was measured — it claims the allocation is now impossible.
